findings.where: Screens 7 and 8, the typed answers for 2(a) and 2(b)
findings.what: The accepted figures 0.37 Ω and 596.59 A are never accepted. The page reads f.accept.also, but K.figure returns no accept field, so also() gives [] (the self-test report lists accept: [] for all three answers). If Dan types 0.37 Ω or 596.59 A he is told 'Not quite' and loses a try, against what the case file promises. Pass the figures explicitly (accept: [0.37] and [596.59]) or make K.figure return accept. While there, fix the 2(a) rightNote, which reads 'That is 0.366 Ω to two places'. Make it '0.37 Ω is 0.366 Ω rounded to two places. Part (b) starts from 0.366 Ω.'

No screen gives the question's key input, 9.22 mΩ/m for a 4 mm² line and cpc. It shows only if Dan picked 4 mm² on screen 3, and never if he skipped to the practice. Part 2(a) states its 14.82 mΩ/m, so state this one too: 'Use 9.22 mΩ/m for the 4 mm² pair.' Choosing the 70 °C multiplier can stay the test.

'It trips on residual current, not on fault current' sets two things against each other that are the same thing: an earth fault current is a residual current. Rewrite it: 'It trips when line and neutral differ by its rating, 30 mA say. So even a poor earth path lets enough current flow to trip it.'

'Table 41.5 allows about 1667 Ω ... Check both figures in BS 7671 before you rely on them' hedges a value that is exact and adds a caveat that doubts the source. Drop 'about' and the last sentence. If research quotes the 50 V ÷ IΔn rule, show it so that 1667 Ω is worked from a rule.

findings.where: Screen 2, What it is for, first sentence
findings.what: 'By now the circuit works.' is vague, so a tired reader stops to ask what 'works' means. Say it plainly: 'The earlier lessons sized the circuit to carry its load.'

findings.where: Section B b2, point 3 (and the same sentence in the model answer)
findings.what: 'The current flows in both line and neutral through it.' does not explain why the RCD stays in. Rewrite it: 'The load current goes out on the line and back on the neutral through it, so it sees no imbalance.'

The current axis is linear from 0 to 1500 A. That puts the whole pass-or-fail story (0 to 250 A) in its bottom sixth. Dragging from 11.4 m to 50 m moves the dot only about 55 px, and the three band labels sit about 15 px apart at 360 px. A log axis, or an axis to about 750 A with the top clamped, would make crossing Ia the big movement.

findings.where: Keep this card, rule and where
findings.what: The card says 'Too high? ... or an RCD' but gives no RCD condition (the Table 41.5 maximum, 1667 Ω at 30 mA). 'Where it lives' names only Table 41.3, yet the practice text checks against Tables 41.2 to 41.4, and fuses need 41.2 and 41.4.

Points 1 and 2 overlap (the voltage can fall to 218.5 V; Cmin 0.95 allows for it), and so do points 4 and 5 (the smallest current must reach Ia; so maximum Zs is worked at Cmin). One sentence can earn two points, so 'any three' can be met with two ideas. Merge or sharpen them.

findings.where: Section B b2, point 2, and the lesson's screens
findings.what: Point 2's first sentence runs to 27 words with a regulation number. Split it: 'A PME earth must not serve an outdoor charge point on its own. One of three measures must hold the open-PEN voltage within 70 V.' No screen mentions EV charging or PEN faults, so this question is pure recall with no refresh before it. A line on screen 5, or a note that it is 18th Edition ground, would help.

Both questions ask whether the value is acceptable, but Dan types only a number (the fault current, or Zs). The comparison a C&G answer expects (0.366 Ω against 0.87 Ω, or 0.925 Ω against 0.87 Ω) appears only in the text that follows. A quick Acceptable or Too high pick after the typed figure would make him make the call.
